Que.q: Q1 : What is Spring Data JPA?
Que.a: Spring Data JPA is a part of the Spring Data project that simplifies database access in Java applications. It provides an abstraction layer on top of JPA (Java Persistence API), reducing boilerplate code and eliminating the need to write repetitive SQL and DAO logic. Developers can directly use repository interfaces and built-in methods for database operations. This allows developers to focus more on business logic rather than database handling details, making development faster, cleaner, and more maintainable in enterprise applications.

Que.q: Q2 : Explain the features of Spring Data JPA.
Que.a: Spring Data JPA provides multiple powerful features that simplify database operations in Java applications. It supports automatic repository implementation, query method generation, pagination, sorting, custom queries using @Query, auditing, and transaction management. It integrates seamlessly with Spring Boot, making configuration easier. It also reduces repetitive database code and improves maintainability. These features help developers build scalable and efficient backend systems with minimal effort.

Que.q: Q3 : How do you create a custom repository in Spring JPA?
Que.a: In Spring JPA, a custom repository is created by defining an interface that extends JpaRepository or CrudRepository. Spring Data JPA automatically generates the implementation at runtime. Developers can also define custom query methods using method naming conventions or @Query annotations. This approach removes the need for writing manual DAO classes and simplifies database interaction significantly.

Que.code: public interface UserRepository extends JpaRepository<User, Long> {}

Que.q: Q4 : What is the difference between CrudRepository and JpaRepository?
Que.a: CrudRepository provides basic CRUD operations such as save, delete, findById, and findAll. JpaRepository extends CrudRepository and adds advanced JPA-specific features such as pagination, sorting, flushing, and batch operations. Because of these additional capabilities, JpaRepository is preferred in most Spring Boot applications for building scalable and production-ready systems.

Que.q: Q5 : How do you write a custom query in Spring JPA?
Que.a: Custom queries in Spring JPA are written using the @Query annotation. This allows developers to define JPQL or native SQL queries directly inside repository interfaces. It is useful when method naming conventions are not sufficient for complex queries. This feature provides flexibility in querying relational databases while still keeping code inside the repository layer.

Que.code: @Query("SELECT u FROM User u WHERE u.firstName = :firstName")

Que.q: Q6 : What is the purpose of the save() method in CrudRepository?
Que.a: The save() method is used to persist an entity in the database. It performs both insert and update operations depending on whether the entity already exists. If the primary key is present, it updates the record; otherwise, it inserts a new one. This makes it a convenient and unified method for handling data persistence in Spring Data JPA applications.

Que.note: save() automatically decides between INSERT and UPDATE based on entity state.

Que.q: Q7 : What is the use of @Modifying annotation?
Que.a: @Modifying annotation is used with @Query when performing update or delete operations in Spring Data JPA. It informs Spring that the query will modify data instead of just reading it. Without this annotation, update and delete queries will not execute properly. It is often used along with transactional support to ensure data consistency.

Que.note: @Modifying is mandatory for update and delete queries in Spring Data JPA.

Que.q: Q8 : What is the difference between findById() and getOne()?
Que.a: findById() immediately fetches data from the database and returns an Optional object. getOne() returns a lazy proxy object and loads the actual data only when it is accessed. If the entity does not exist, getOne() may throw an exception when the proxy is accessed. Because of this behavior, findById() is safer and more commonly used.

Que.q: Q9 : What is the use of @Temporal annotation?
Que.a: @Temporal annotation is used to define how date and time values are stored in the database. It is applied to Date or Calendar fields to specify whether only date, only time, or full timestamp should be stored. This ensures correct mapping between Java date types and database date formats.

Que.note: Used with TemporalType.DATE, TIME, or TIMESTAMP.

Que.q: Q10 : How do you write a query method for sorting in Spring Data JPA?
Que.a: Sorting in Spring Data JPA can be achieved using method naming conventions like OrderBy or by using Sort parameter. It allows results to be returned in ascending or descending order based on entity fields. This makes it easy to control data ordering without writing explicit SQL queries.

Que.q: Q11 : Explain @Transactional annotation in Spring.
Que.a: @Transactional annotation is used to manage database transactions in Spring applications. It ensures that a group of operations are executed as a single unit of work. If all operations succeed, the transaction is committed; if any exception occurs, the entire transaction is rolled back automatically. This guarantees data consistency and integrity, especially in critical operations like banking, order processing, or multi-step database updates where partial execution is not acceptable.

Que.note: If any step fails inside a @Transactional method, all changes are rolled back automatically.

Que.q: Q12 : Difference between FetchType.EAGER and FetchType.LAZY?
Que.a: FetchType defines how related entities are loaded in JPA. EAGER loading fetches related data immediately along with the main entity, even if it is not required. LAZY loading fetches related data only when it is accessed, which improves performance and reduces memory usage. In real-world applications, LAZY loading is generally preferred because it avoids unnecessary database queries and improves system efficiency.

Que.q: Q13 : What is the use of @Id annotation?
Que.a: @Id annotation is used to define the primary key of an entity in Spring JPA. It uniquely identifies each record in a database table. Every entity must have a primary key field annotated with @Id so that JPA can manage object persistence correctly and maintain entity identity within the persistence context.

Que.note: Every JPA entity must contain exactly one primary key defined using @Id.

Que.q: Q14 : How do you create a composite primary key in Spring JPA?
Que.a: A composite primary key is used when a combination of multiple fields uniquely identifies a record. In Spring JPA, it is implemented using @Embeddable and @EmbeddedId annotations. A separate key class is created to define the composite structure, which is then embedded into the entity. This approach ensures proper mapping of complex keys in relational databases.

Que.q: Q15 : What is the use of @EnableJpaRepositories annotation?
Que.a: @EnableJpaRepositories is used to enable JPA repository scanning in Spring applications. It tells Spring where to find repository interfaces and automatically generates their implementations at runtime. This annotation is usually placed in configuration classes and helps bootstrap Spring Data JPA support in the application context.

Que.q: Q16 : Rules for defining custom repository methods?
Que.a: Spring Data JPA allows automatic query generation based on method names. Custom repository methods must follow naming conventions such as findBy, countBy, deleteBy, or existsBy, followed by entity field names. Logical keywords like And, Or, Between, and OrderBy can also be used to build complex queries without writing SQL.

Que.q: Q17 : Explain Query By Example (QBE) in Spring Data JPA.
Que.a: Query By Example (QBE) is a dynamic query technique where an example entity is created with sample values. Spring Data JPA automatically builds queries based on non-null fields of the example object. It eliminates the need for writing explicit queries and is useful for simple dynamic search requirements.

Que.note: QBE is useful for dynamic filtering without writing SQL or JPQL.

Que.q: Q18 : What is pagination in Spring Data JPA?
Que.a: Pagination is used to divide large datasets into smaller, manageable pages. In Spring Data JPA, it is implemented using Pageable and Page interfaces. Developers can define page number, page size, and sorting criteria to efficiently fetch data. This improves performance by reducing memory usage and avoiding loading large datasets at once.

Que.q: Q19 : Commonly used CrudRepository methods?
Que.a: CrudRepository provides basic methods to interact with the database such as saving entities, retrieving records, deleting data, and counting records. These methods help eliminate boilerplate code and simplify CRUD operations in Spring applications.

Que.q: Q20 : Difference between delete() and deleteInBatch()?
Que.a: The delete() method removes a single entity at a time, whereas deleteInBatch() removes multiple entities in a single batch operation. Batch deletion is more efficient because it reduces database calls and improves performance when dealing with large datasets. However, deleteInBatch() should be used carefully because it bypasses some entity lifecycle events.

Que.note: deleteInBatch() is faster but bypasses some JPA lifecycle callbacks.

Que.q: Q21 : How do you execute complex queries involving multiple tables in Spring JPA?
Que.a: Complex queries in Spring JPA are executed using the @Query annotation with JPQL or native SQL. These queries support joins, subqueries, aggregations, and multi-table operations. JPQL is preferred for database independence, while native SQL is used when advanced or database-specific features are required. This approach gives flexibility while keeping query logic inside repository interfaces.

Que.q: Q22 : How do you optimize batch insertion in Spring JPA?
Que.a: Batch insertion in Spring JPA is optimized by enabling Hibernate batch processing using configuration properties like hibernate.jdbc.batch_size. This groups multiple insert operations into a single batch, reducing database round trips and improving performance significantly. It is especially useful when inserting large datasets such as logs, transactions, or bulk user records.

Que.note: Batch processing improves performance by reducing database communication overhead.

Que.q: Q23 : How do you manage bidirectional relationships in Spring JPA?
Que.a: Bidirectional relationships in Spring JPA are managed using @OneToMany, @ManyToOne, and mappedBy attributes. These mappings define how entities are connected in both directions. To prevent infinite loops during JSON serialization, annotations like @JsonManagedReference and @JsonBackReference are used. Proper relationship mapping ensures data integrity and efficient entity navigation.

Que.q: Q24 : How do you handle schema migration in Spring JPA projects?
Que.a: Schema migration in Spring JPA is handled using tools like Flyway or Liquibase. These tools manage database changes using versioned scripts that run automatically during application startup. This ensures that database schema stays synchronized with application code across different environments like development, testing, and production.

Que.note: Flyway and Liquibase help maintain version control for database schema changes.

Que.q: Q25 : How do you implement caching in Spring JPA?
Que.a: Caching in Spring JPA is implemented using Spring Cache abstraction along with providers like Redis, EHCache, or Hazelcast. Frequently accessed data is stored in cache memory to reduce repeated database calls. This improves application performance and reduces database load significantly, especially in high-traffic systems.

Que.note: Caching reduces database load by storing frequently accessed data in memory.

Que.q: Q26 : What is JPA in Java?
Que.a: JPA (Java Persistence API) is a specification used for object-relational mapping in Java. It provides a standard way to map Java objects to database tables. Instead of writing complex SQL queries, developers use JPA annotations and APIs to perform database operations in an object-oriented manner, making development simpler and more maintainable.

Que.note: JPA is only a specification; Hibernate is one of its implementations.

Que.q: Q27 : What is Hibernate in Spring JPA?
Que.a: Hibernate is a popular implementation of the JPA specification that provides ORM capabilities. It automatically maps Java objects to database tables and handles SQL generation, caching, lazy loading, and transaction management. Hibernate reduces boilerplate code and simplifies database interaction in enterprise Java applications.

Que.q: Q28 : What is ORM in Spring JPA?
Que.a: ORM (Object Relational Mapping) is a technique that maps Java objects to relational database tables. It allows developers to interact with databases using objects instead of SQL queries. ORM frameworks like Hibernate handle the conversion between object models and relational data automatically.

Que.note: ORM eliminates the need to write manual SQL for most CRUD operations.

Que.q: Q29 : What is the use of @Entity annotation in Spring JPA?
Que.a: The @Entity annotation marks a Java class as a JPA entity that is mapped to a database table. Spring JPA uses this annotation to identify classes that should be persisted in the database. Each entity represents a table, and each object represents a row in that table.

Que.note: Every entity class must be annotated with @Entity for JPA to manage it.

Que.q: Q30 : What is the use of @Table annotation in Spring JPA?
Que.a: The @Table annotation is used to define the database table name associated with a JPA entity. If not specified, Spring JPA uses the class name as the table name by default. It also allows configuration of schema, unique constraints, and table-level metadata for better database control.

Que.note: @Table is optional but useful for customizing table mapping.

Que.q: Q31 : What is the use of @Column annotation in Spring JPA?
Que.a: @Column annotation is used to map a Java entity field to a database table column. It allows customization of column properties such as name, length, nullable constraint, uniqueness, and default values. This annotation gives fine-grained control over how entity fields are stored in the database, ensuring proper schema design and validation rules at the database level.

Que.q: Q32 : What is the use of @GeneratedValue annotation?
Que.a: @GeneratedValue annotation is used to automatically generate primary key values for entities in Spring JPA. It eliminates the need for manual ID assignment. It supports multiple strategies like AUTO, IDENTITY, SEQUENCE, and TABLE, depending on database capabilities. This ensures consistent and unique identifier generation for each entity record.

list.4: TABLE → Uses a separate table for IDs

Que.q: Q33 : Difference between @OneToOne and @OneToMany relationships?
Que.a: @OneToOne relationship means one entity instance is associated with exactly one instance of another entity. @OneToMany means one entity is associated with multiple instances of another entity. These mappings help represent real-world relationships in database design using object-oriented principles.

Que.q: Q34 : What is the use of @ManyToOne annotation?
Que.a: @ManyToOne annotation defines a relationship where multiple entities are associated with a single parent entity. It is commonly used in relational database modeling to represent hierarchical relationships such as employees belonging to a department.

Que.note: ManyToOne is the most frequently used relationship in JPA mappings.

Que.q: Q35 : What is the use of @JoinColumn annotation?
Que.a: @JoinColumn annotation is used to define the foreign key column in a relationship mapping. It specifies how two tables are connected in the database. It is typically used in @OneToOne, @OneToMany, and @ManyToOne relationships to establish proper table relationships.

Que.note: @JoinColumn defines the foreign key column in relational mapping.

Que.q: Q36 : What is lazy loading in Hibernate?
Que.a: Lazy loading is a performance optimization technique where related entities are loaded only when they are accessed. Instead of fetching all related data immediately, Hibernate delays loading until it is required. This reduces unnecessary database queries and improves application performance.

Que.note: Lazy loading helps reduce memory usage and improves performance.

Que.q: Q37 : What is eager loading in Hibernate?
Que.a: Eager loading fetches all related entities immediately along with the main entity. This ensures data is readily available but may lead to performance overhead due to unnecessary data retrieval. It is useful when related data is always required.

list.4: Useful when data is always needed

Que.q: Q38 : What is JPQL in Spring JPA?
Que.a: JPQL (Java Persistence Query Language) is an object-oriented query language used in JPA. It works with entity classes and their fields instead of database tables. JPQL is database-independent and allows writing portable queries across different database systems.

Que.note: JPQL queries are written using entity names, not table names.

Que.q: Q39 : Difference between JPQL and native SQL queries?
Que.a: JPQL is object-oriented and works with entity classes, while native SQL works directly with database tables. JPQL is database-independent, making it portable across systems. Native SQL is database-specific and is used when advanced or performance-critical queries are required.

Que.q: Q40 : What is the persistence context in JPA?
Que.a: Persistence context is a first-level cache managed by JPA that tracks entity objects during a transaction. It ensures that any changes made to entities are automatically synchronized with the database. It improves performance by reducing repeated database calls and maintains consistency between Java objects and database state.

Que.note: Persistence context automatically tracks entity state changes within a transaction.

Que.q: Q41 : What are the different entity states in JPA?
Que.a: In JPA, entities pass through different lifecycle states: Transient, Persistent, Detached, and Removed. Transient objects are simple Java objects not associated with the persistence context. Persistent objects are managed by JPA and synchronized with the database. Detached objects were once persistent but are no longer tracked. Removed entities are marked for deletion from the database during transaction commit.

Que.q: Q42 : What is dirty checking in Hibernate?
Que.a: Dirty checking is a Hibernate mechanism that automatically detects changes made to persistent entities within a transaction. Hibernate compares the original state of an entity with its current state and updates the database if changes are found. This removes the need for explicit update queries and simplifies data persistence logic.

Que.note: Dirty checking happens automatically during transaction commit in Hibernate.

Que.q: Q43 : What is cascading in JPA?
Que.a: Cascading in JPA allows operations performed on a parent entity to automatically propagate to its associated child entities. This ensures consistency across related entities and reduces manual database operations. Common cascade types include PERSIST, MERGE, REMOVE, REFRESH, DETACH, and ALL.

Que.q: Q44 : What is orphanRemoval in JPA?
Que.a: orphanRemoval is a JPA feature that automatically deletes child entities when they are removed from their parent entity relationship. It helps maintain database integrity by preventing orphan records from remaining in the database when they are no longer associated with any parent.

Que.note: orphanRemoval = true ensures child entities are deleted when removed from parent.

Que.q: Q45 : What is optimistic locking in JPA?
Que.a: Optimistic locking is a concurrency control technique used to prevent conflicts when multiple transactions update the same record. It uses a version field annotated with @Version to track changes. If another transaction modifies the record, an exception is thrown to avoid overwriting data.

Que.note: Optimistic locking is best for systems with fewer write conflicts.

Que.q: Q46 : What is pessimistic locking in JPA?
Que.a: Pessimistic locking locks database records during a transaction to prevent other transactions from modifying them until the lock is released. This ensures strong consistency but may reduce performance due to blocked access in concurrent systems.

Que.note: Pessimistic locking is useful in high-conflict scenarios like banking systems.

Que.q: Q47 : What is the N+1 query problem in Hibernate?
Que.a: The N+1 query problem occurs when Hibernate executes one query to fetch parent entities and then executes additional queries for each associated child entity. This leads to performance degradation due to excessive database calls. It can be solved using JOIN FETCH, EntityGraph, or batch fetching strategies.

Que.q: Q48 : What is EntityManager in JPA?
Que.a: EntityManager is the core interface in JPA used to interact with the persistence context. It manages entity lifecycle operations such as persist, merge, remove, find, and refresh. It acts as a bridge between Java objects and the database, enabling ORM functionality.

Que.q: Q49 : What are the advantages of Spring Data JPA?
Que.a: Spring Data JPA simplifies database access by reducing boilerplate code and providing built-in repository support. It offers automatic query generation, pagination, sorting, transaction management, auditing, and seamless integration with Spring Boot. It improves productivity and makes applications easier to maintain and scale.

Que.q: Q50 : Why is Spring Data JPA widely used in enterprise applications?
Que.a: Spring Data JPA is widely used in enterprise applications because it simplifies database interaction, supports scalable architecture, and integrates seamlessly with Spring Boot. It reduces development time, improves maintainability, and provides powerful ORM capabilities suitable for complex business systems like banking, e-commerce, and SaaS platforms.

Que.note: It is preferred in enterprise systems due to scalability, productivity, and strong ORM support.
